text:
Charlie Coyle hasn't had a point in six games, and Columbus hasn't won in five. Put those two facts side by side and it looks like a 34-year-old fading. Look closer and it's one of the unluckiest stretches in the league.

Columbus gets 55.6% of the 5v5 expected goals (the quality of chances) with Coyle on the ice, almost 11 points better than when he sits. He's playing nearly 20 minutes a night and still getting to the net: three goals on 5.4 expected, and 4.9 expected goals' worth of chances in the pointless run alone. The Blue Jackets have scored 9.7 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him out there, and by wins added from goals he ranks 522nd of 542 skaters, which is mostly a measure of bad bounces.

Evolving-Hockey had him 58th of 401 forwards last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put him in the 90th percentile for primary shot assists. The Columbus team around him is the bigger worry right now. Coyle's own game looks like it's waiting for the puck to start going in.
headline: Coyle is doing the work and getting nothing
